title: Workload portrait & batcher policy automation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an automated policy engine that synthesizes a compact 'workload portrait' for each customer/route and uses it to safely propose and apply continuous batching and cache parameters. The portrait should capture request-size distributions, temporal burstiness, cold-start patterns, KV/prefix reuse rates, and SLO/cost sensitivities.

Motivation: Customers with variable traffic waste GPU cycles when conservative batch sizes are applied globally. A per-workload portrait + heuristic policy lets us reduce unit cost while bounding tail latency and error impact. Must include safe deployment primitives (shadow apply, canary, automated rollback) and observable guardrails so SREs/PMs can audit changes.

High-level approach:
- Profiling: lightweight agent aggregates per-route metrics (small quantiles, histograms for sequence length, inter-arrival times, cache hit rates) and uploads compressed profiles to the recommendation service on a cadence and on trigger events (e.g., 3x burst).
- Portrait synthesis: summarize long-tail behaviors into a compact signature (e.g., 7 features: median seq length, 95th seq length, p99 inter-arrival, burstiness score, kv-key reuse ratio, cold-start rate, percentage of requests below 64 tokens).
- Heuristics & policy rules: rules map portrait fingerprints to safe candidate parameter sets (batch size, max latency target, batching window, preferred quantization profile, prefix-cache TTL). Rules include conservative defaults, isolation for high-variance portraits, and cost-aware aggressors for stable portraits. Rules are human-auditable and versioned.
- Continuous tuning loop: the recommendation engine proposes shadow configurations and runs them against mirrored traffic. If shadow metrics (p50/p95 latency, tail tokens/sec, error rate, token-cost delta) meet thresholds, the engine offers a canary rollout (small percentage) with automated monitors for regressions. If regressions are detected, the system can auto-rollback to the prior config and create an incident with telemetry.
- Safe apply mechanics: 1) shadow apply, 2) canary (1-5% traffic) with extended observation windows, 3) staged ramp to target, 4) automated rollback triggers. All changes are logged and tied to a rollout object in Console.

Non-goals: model-selection/architecture changes, deep model-level kernel rewrites. This ticket focuses on the control-plane: portraits, heuristics, rollout safety, and observability integration.
acceptance_criteria: Profile agent implemented and shipping compact portraits for >=90% of active routes (agent uses <=2% CPU on sidecars and compresses profiles before upload)
Recommendation service can generate candidate parameter sets for a given portrait fingerprint and export them as recommended_rollout objects
Shadow apply mechanism implemented: recommended configuration can be executed in shadow mode and generate side-by-side metrics (latency, cost delta, error rate) in the console
Canary rollout automation: system can promote a candidate to canary (1-5% traffic) with monitor windows and automated rollback on defined thresholds
Dashboard and audit trail: every proposed and applied config has an entry in Console with before/after metrics, owner, and changelog
Unit & integration tests for heuristic rules and rollback triggers with >=90% coverage for rule engine paths
tasks: Spike: implement profiling agent prototype and collect portraits for 50 routes (2 weeks)
Design: formalize portrait feature set and serialization format (proto) and publish spec in Confluence
Engine: implement rule engine that maps portraits to candidate batch/cache params (include versioning)
Runtime: add shadow-apply plumbing to runtime to accept mirrored configs and emit shadow metrics
Console: surface recommendations and rollout objects in the Rollouts page with audit links
Safety: implement canary ramp automation and rollback triggers wired into on-call runbooks
E2E: run staged experiment on staging and then small set of low-risk production routes before general availability

2026-02-20 Tom Nguyen: Spike update - profiler prototype collected good KV reuse signals; memory overhead on sidecar is ~1.4MB per route. Uploaded compressed portraits to toy recommendation service. See profiling logs linked.

2026-03-02 Lena Ortiz (Design): Reviewed portrait UX. Recommended adding a 'stability' flag to portrait so heuristics can be more conservative for bursty customers. Also suggested 'explainability' strings for each recommended change so PMs can review why a change was suggested.

2026-03-08 Marcus Chen (SRE): Safety checklist - must ensure shadow apply cannot change persistence or encryption settings. Also, rollback windows should default to 30m for latency-sensitive routes and 2h for cost-first routes.
